title: Targeted Plasma Proteomics Reveals a Central Role of Upregulated TNFRSF Proteins in HIV-associated Stroke: A Cross-sectional Discovery and Longitudinal Validation Study
projectDescription: This study investigated circulating proteomic signatures associated with stroke in people with HIV (PWH) using a nested case–control design. Plasma samples were collected from 135 HIV-positive individuals with stroke (HIV+/Stroke+), 135 HIV-positive stroke-free controls (HIV+/Stroke−), and 135 HIV-negative stroke-free controls (HIV−/Stroke−) from the CHART cohort (Taizhou, China). A longitudinal sub-cohort of 37 HIV+/Stroke+ individuals with paired pre- and post-stroke samples was additionally included for temporal validation. All plasma samples were profiled using the Olink Target 96 Cardiovascular II and Cardiovascular III panels simultaneously, quantifying 184 non-overlapping protein biomarkers. The study aimed to identify stroke-associated proteomic signatures, characterise underlying biological pathways and protein interaction networks, and validate key proteins longitudinally.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Venous blood samples were collected in EDTA tubes and processed within two hours of collection. Plasma was obtained by centrifugation at 2000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C, aliquoted, and stored at −80°C until analysis. Plasma protein abundance was measured using the Olink Target 96 Proximity Extension Assay (PEA) technology on two complementary panels: Cardiovascular II and Cardiovascular III, each quantifying 92 proteins simultaneously. All samples were profiled on both panels in parallel. Each sample was assessed using four internal controls per assay (two incubation controls, one extension control, and one detection control). Each plate included three inter-plate controls (IPCs), three negative controls, and duplicate pooled plasma reference samples. Longitudinally paired samples from the same individual were assigned to the same assay plate to eliminate within-subject plate effects.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw proximity extension assay data were processed using Olink Intensity Normalization v.2. Intra-plate normalisation was performed using internal extension controls; inter-plate normalisation was achieved by aligning plate-specific medians to a global median reference. Protein abundance was reported in Normalized Protein eXpression (NPX) units on a log2 scale. Internal quality control thresholds were applied: plate standard deviation < 0.2 NPX and individual sample deviation < 0.3 NPX. Intra-assay coefficient of variation (CV) was 4% for both panels; inter-assay CV was 11% and 10% for Cardiovascular II and III, respectively. Samples below the limit of detection (LOD) were retained in accordance with Olink official guidelines, with the proportion of sub-LOD values reported in the Source Data file.
